docs.title: Welcome to Tomiio's Blog
docs.text:
Hello and thanks for visiting my blog! Here, I share my experiences, projects, and insights on topics like embedded systems, robotics, programming, and more. Whether you're a fellow developer, hobbyist, or just curious, I hope you'll find something interesting and useful.

This blog is my way of sharing stories from my journey—documenting the challenges, discoveries, and lessons learned through my projects.

Check out my projects at: - 11/2022 - Autonomous Driving Vehicle. - 07/2023 - BLDC Driver (FOC - Field Oriented Control). - 10/2023 - Handsignator (Deaf-mute disablities support device). - 10/2025 - Autonomous Wheelchair

docs.title: Autonomous Driving Vehicle
docs.text: • Being update!!! ...

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation of my Autonomous Driving Vehicle project developed for the Bosch Future Mobility Challenge (BFMC). This project is a 1:10 scale autonomous car platform designed to perform real-world driving tasks such as traffic signs perception, lane keeping, obstacle avoidance, intersection handling, and autonomous parking.

docs.title: 2. Objectives
docs.text:
• Compete in the BFMC competition.
  • Develop a robust autonomous driving stack combining perception, planning, and control based on Sensors (Camera, Distance Sensor) and Actuators (BLDC Motor and Servo).
  • Integrate embedded hardware (STM32F401RE Nucleo, Jetson Xavier NX) with ROS.
  • Demonstrate safe and reliable driving behavior in a constrained track environment.
  • The vehicle should be able to perform the challenges:
    • Lane keeping
    • Follow the traffic rules detected from traffic signs
    • Obstacle avoidance (Pedestrians and Other Vehicles on road)
    • Intersection handling
    • Autonomous parking
    • Complete the planned path by localization and navigation

docs.title: 3.1 Computing Units
docs.text:
• NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX
    • Runs Ubuntu + ROS
    • Executes vision, AI inference, and planning
  • STM32F401RE
    • Handles low-level motor and steering control
    • Interfaces with sensors (IMU, encoder, ultrasonic)

docs.title: 3.2 Sensors
docs.text: Sensor Purpose Camera (Logitech C922) Lane detection, sign detection IMU Vehicle orientation and angular velocity Wheel encoder Velocity estimation Ultrasonic sensor Obstacle distance

docs.title: 3.3 Actuators
docs.text:
• BLDC motor + ESC (longitudinal control)
  • Servo motor (steering, Ackermann geometry)

docs.title: 4. System Architecture
docs.text:
The system is divided into the following modules:

4.1. Perception - Lane detection (camera-based, OpenCV/ML). - Obstacle detection (ultrasonic sensors, LiDAR). - Sign & traffic light recognition.

4.2. Planning - Behavior planner (FSM-based). - Global/local path generation. - Obstacle avoidance & lane switching.

4.3. Control - Low-level motor + steering control (PID & Stanley/MPC). - Safety overrides & emergency stop.

4.4. Hardware - Car chassis: 1:10 RC model with differential steering. - SBC: Raspberry Pi 5 + Jetson Xavier NX (vision & ML tasks). - MCU: STM32F4 for motor control + sensor integration. - Sensors: Camera, ultrasonic, IMU, wheel encoders.

docs.title: 5.2 ROS Topics
docs.text: Topic Description /automobile/image_raw Camera image /lane/midpoint Lane center position /detected_objects YOLO detection results /automobile/command Speed & steering command

docs.title: 6.1 Overview
docs.text: The Perception module provides real-time environmental understanding for the autonomous vehicle. Its primary functions include lane detection, object and traffic sign recognition, traffic light state estimation, and intersection detection. The output of this module supplies structured information to the planning and control layers through ROS topics.

docs.title: 6.2 Input and Pre-processing
docs.text: A forward-facing RGB camera is used as the primary perception sensor. Captured frames are pre-processed using grayscale conversion, Gaussian filtering, and edge enhancement to improve robustness against noise and illumination variation.

docs.title: 6.3 Lane Detection Methodology
docs.text:
Lane detection is implemented using a classical computer vision pipeline combined with clustering:

  • Edge extraction is performed using Sobel and Canny operators.
  • Line candidates are extracted using the Hough Transform.
  • DBSCAN clustering groups fragmented lane segments and removes noise.
  • Left and right lane boundaries are identified, and the lane center is computed as the midpoint.

The method supports both solid and dashed lane markings and provides a stable middle-point reference for lateral control.

docs.title: 6.4 Illumination Handling
docs.text: To reduce the impact of glare and uneven lighting, histogram-based intensity correction is applied during pre-processing. This step improves the reliability of both lane detection and object recognition under challenging lighting conditions.

docs.title: 6.5 Object and Traffic Sign Detection
docs.text:
Object detection is performed using a YOLOv8 deep learning model fine-tuned on a custom dataset. Detected objects include traffic signs, vehicles, pedestrians, traffic lights, and intersections.

To improve classification accuracy for traffic signs, a lightweight secondary classifier is applied to verify YOLO detections.

docs.title: 6.6 Traffic Light Recognition
docs.text: Traffic light states are determined either directly through the detection model or via image-based color analysis within detected traffic light regions. This hybrid approach ensures robust recognition while maintaining real-time performance.

docs.title: 6.7 Intersection Detection
docs.text: Intersections are detected by combining visual features from the perception pipeline with vehicle localization data. This information is used to determine feasible maneuvers and is forwarded to the planning module.

docs.title: 6.8 ROS-Based Integration
docs.text: The perception system is implemented as a set of ROS nodes, each responsible for a specific task such as image acquisition, lane detection, or object recognition. Communication between nodes is handled through standard ROS topics, enabling modularity and scalability.

docs.title: 6.9 Summary
docs.text: The perception module integrates classical vision techniques and deep learning to deliver reliable lane, object, and intersection information. Its modular ROS-based design allows real-time operation and seamless integration with planning and control components.
